title: SecOps-NG Contractual-Obligations Evidence Artifact
description: Typed shape for one evidence artifact emitted by the contractual-obligations evidence stream (F-WF-10). One artifact is produced per execution of the contractual-obligations tracker workflow against a single supplier-contract reference; it enumerates the obligations the operator has accepted from that contract and the per-obligation review schedule the workflow derived. Discharges the contract-time half of NIS2 Article 21(2)(d) (per-entity supply-chain risk management — security characteristics of direct suppliers and service providers with periodic re-attestation) and complements the execution-time F-CP-03 supply-chain stream which captures the dependency surface a workflow resolved against at runtime. The two streams share no key by design (this stream keys on `contract_id`; F-CP-03 keys on `(workflow_id, execution_id)`); a CORE-FANOUT sibling will pin the cross-stream join on `supplier_ref` <-> `provider_id` once both surfaces are at CORE. Public-bar artifact: supplier identifiers are opaque operator-side ids, operator-side strings (owner labels, clause refs) MUST stay role-shaped or URN-shaped, and individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3. SKELETON layer: required-field shape and the high-level `contract`, `obligations[]`, and `review_schedule[]` envelopes are pinned so the CORE-FANOUT sibling cards can bind primitive emitters against a stable contract; inner object shapes are intentionally permissive at this layer and tightened in EXTEND-schema.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject artifacts produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship. SKELETON layer carries 0.1.0; the EXTEND-schema sibling card lifts it to 1.0.0 once inner envelopes are tightened.

artifact_id.description: Stable per-artifact identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<workflow_id>|<execution_id>|<contract.contract_id>|<captured_at>` (UTF-8, no separators around the pipes). Two executions of the same workflow at the same instant against the same contract collide deliberately; the same execution re-emitted at the same captured_at stays byte-identical.

stream.description: Identifies which evidence stream produced the artifact. Constant on this schema.

workflow_id.description: Stable workflow identifier — one of the workflow ids declared under `content/playbooks/<workflow-id>/`. The F-WF-10 SKELETON anchor is `contractual_obligations_tracker`.

execution_id.description: Per-execution identifier issued by the compile target's workflow runtime (n8n execution id, Temporal workflow run id, LangGraph thread/checkpoint id). Re-runs of the same workflow_id produce distinct execution_ids.

regulation_refs.description: Pins to the upstream regulatory mapping entries this artifact helps satisfy (typically `nis2:art-21-2-d` plus, where applicable, `nis2:art-22` for the Union-level Cooperation-Group overlay). At least one entry — an artifact with no regulatory anchor is not evidence in the F-WF-10 sense. Joins back into content/mappings/<regime>/*.yaml via the `id` field.

control_refs.description: Control stable-ids attested by this artifact. At least one — typically `control.supplier_inventory@v1` and `control.provider_attestation@v1`.

contract.description: The normalised supplier-contract record the workflow ingested on this execution.

contract_id.description: Stable operator-side identifier for the contract record (e.g. `contract.supplier-x.master-services@v1`). The contract catalogue is operator-supplied; the framework ships the schema, not the catalogue. Public-bar text: opaque operator id, no commercial brand names baked into the schema.

supplier_ref.description: Stable operator-side identifier for the supplier the contract is with. Same shape vocabulary as F-CP-03's `provider_id` (`provider.<id>@v<n>`) so the cross-stream join can be wired up at CORE without a schema rename. Where the supplier is also a runtime provider, `supplier_ref` and `provider_id` SHOULD agree.

effective_at.description: ISO-8601 date on which the contract took effect.

expires_at.description: ISO-8601 date on which the contract expires. `null` for evergreen / open-ended contracts.

jurisdiction.description: ISO-3166 alpha-2 country code for the governing-law jurisdiction the contract names. The SKELETON layer treats this as advisory; the EXTEND-schema sibling card tightens it once cross-border-transfer scoring is folded into the artifact.

obligations.description: One record per obligation the operator has accepted from this contract. Empty array is invalid — an obligation-evidence artifact for a contract with zero extracted obligations should not be emitted at all. SKELETON layer carries a permissive inner shape; EXTEND-schema tightens the clause-reference and obligation-kind vocabularies.

review_schedule.description: One record per obligation declared in `obligations[]`, in the same order. Carries the per-obligation review schedule the workflow derived from the obligation's contractual cadence and the operator's review-policy.

owner.description: Dated ownership pointer for the supplier-inventory control attestation. Role-shaped — a working-group mailbox, a generic role title, or a community handle. Individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected here as a matter of schema discipline.

role.description: Generic role or working-group identifier (e.g. 'supplier-governance@example.org', 'procurement-lead', 'contracts-on-call'). Personal names are not used.

assigned_at.description: ISO-8601 date on which the role was assigned ownership of the contractual-obligations attestation chain.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which this artifact was captured. Stable input to the artifact_id derivation so re-emissions in the same execution at the same instant stay byte-identical.

provenance.description: Where this artifact came from. Mirrors the provenance pattern used by content/evidence/*/schemas/* so a reviewer can re-derive the chain back to source.

source_url.description: URL of the workflow run (or workflow-content source) that produced this artifact. Compile targets may use their own run-id URLs; the URL itself is opaque to this schema.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 date or date-time matching the artifact-level captured_at.

commit_sha.description: Optional commit SHA of the content snapshot the workflow walked.

retention.description: Optional retention pointer the operator declares for this evidentiary record. ISO-8601 duration. The community-default value is an open question to be settled in the EXTEND sibling card, mirroring the equivalent F-CP-02 / F-CP-03 / F-CP-04 deferrals.

obligation_record.description: One obligation the operator has accepted from this contract. SKELETON layer pins clause_ref, obligation_kind, and text; the inner envelopes for cadence / scope / waiver are tightened in EXTEND-schema.

obligation_id.description: Stable per-contract identifier for the obligation (e.g. `obligation.audit-right`, `obligation.attestation-cadence`). Operator-supplied; the framework ships the schema, not the catalogue.

clause_ref.description: Reference into the source contract where the obligation lives (e.g. 'cl-8.4', 'annex-2/§3'). Free-text shape at the SKELETON layer; the EXTEND-schema sibling card tightens this to a stable clause-ref grammar.

obligation_kind.description: Which kind of obligation this is. SKELETON-layer enum; the EXTEND-schema sibling card lifts this into a shared vocabulary at schemas/contractual_obligation_kind.json once the cross-stream join with F-CP-03 lands.

text.description: Operator-canonicalised obligation text. No commentary, no rewrites at the SKELETON layer; the EXTEND-schema sibling card pins a canonicalisation pass once the per-target emitters are worked through. Public-bar text: no individual names, no operator branding.

cadence.description: Contractual cadence the clause itself declares for the obligation (e.g. 'P1Y' for annual attestation, 'PT0S' for immediate breach notification). ISO-8601 duration. `null` when the clause carries no explicit cadence — the schedule then falls back to the operator's review-policy.

review_record.description: Per-obligation review schedule, paired one-to-one with the `obligations[]` array. SKELETON layer pins the next-review-due timestamp and the state; the EXTEND-schema sibling card pins the waiver / deferral envelope.

obligation_id.description: Pointer to the matching `obligations[].obligation_id` in this artifact.

state.description: Current review state for the obligation. SKELETON-layer enum mirroring the F-CP-03 attestation_state vocabulary; the EXTEND-schema sibling card lifts this into a shared vocabulary at schemas/obligation_review_state.json.

last_reviewed_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the most recent review event for this obligation. `null` when no review has taken place yet (newly-extracted obligation; state is then 'unknown').

next_review_due_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the next review falls due. The supplier-attestation-staleness KRI (queued in F-WF-10 EXTEND-metrics) fires when (artifact captured_at > next_review_due_at).
